newsitem.title: USA: US March S&P 500 hits new daily high late, ends up.
newsitem.headline: US March S&P 500 hits new daily high late, ends up.

text.p: Feb 7 - U.S. March S&P 500 hit a new daily high at 794.70 late and ended sharply higher. Traders eyed resistance now at Wednesday's high of 796.60 and at 799.70, the all-time and contract high. One trader called the midday slump an "overreaction" and said the rejection of the day's low provided much momentum to the upside.
He said once buying developed near the lows, the underlying bullish tone of the market sprang into action.
"We broke them down on a lack of bid and once we got down there, we found plenty of buyers," another S&P 500 trader said.
The trader noted sell-stops below 782.10 that took March S&Ps to the day's low. On the subsequent rally, buy-stops were triggered at 784.50 to 785.00, he said.
Traders tied the slump to comments from U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that pressured T-bonds and the dollar.

Rubin said he believed in a strong dollar, but the dollar has been strong "for some time," sparking concerns the Clinton Administration may be backing off from its strong dollar policy ahead of Saturday's G7 meeting in Berlin.

Before the setback on the Rubin comments, U.S. assets had rallied strongly on January payrolls data. Traders took the details of that report to mean the Fed would remain on hold and not raise short-term interest rates.
March S&Ps rallied as high as 793.75 in line with T-bond and dollar strength after the payrolls report.
Jobs rose 271,000 after a December rise of 261,000.
Wall Street had forecast a jobs rise of 237,000. The average workweek declined, and hourly earnings rose far less than expected.
Overall, traders called the session choppy and chaotic.
"It was brutal," one S&P broker said. "There were programs on both ways and a lack of liquidity on the upside," he said. "It was tough to get stuff done."
Traders eyed upside targets of 796.60, Wednesday's high, and 799.70, the all-time high.
"The 800 handle looms in our future -- probably next week," one broker said.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 11.70 at 794.35, Value Lines were 5.70 higher at 708.00, NYSE Composites were 4.90 higher at 416.20, Nikkeis were 280 lower at 17,800, Midcap 400s were up 2.10 at 265.80 and Nasdaq 100s were up 15.70 at 906.70.
